source: Source-informed VPM app registry, service lifecycle, token lease, option snapshots, credential adapters, Auth response projections, user-management plans, token verification policy, key caching, signature adaptation, Auth request dispatch, HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 request plans, HTTP/2 session ownership, retry policy, authorization-header ownership and HTTP response projection, plus Firestore client configuration and registry ownership, and per-client Storage context, alongside retained Firebase Admin 14.5.0 service implementations. Upstream source and tests informed compatibility; diagnostics and public declarations remain attributed. Google Auth is a separately tracked upstream-derived dependency. This is not a clean-room claim.

omittedDependencies.@firebase/database-compat: Realtime Database client and its websocket tree; serves only firebase-admin/database.
omittedDependencies.@firebase/database-types: Types for the Realtime Database client.
omittedDependencies.@fastify/busboy: Parses multipart/mixed responses, which no Admin 14 API requests or reads.
omittedDependencies.fast-deep-equal: App option equality uses a bounded-stack comparison of detached records.

changes: Concurrent token verifications share one public-key request while the keys are missing or expired (ID tokens and session cookies via Google certificates, App Check and phone-number verification via JWKS). Upstream sends one request per caller.
HTTP/2 requests (FCM sends) carry the bare :scheme pseudo-header required by RFC 9113. Upstream sends "https:", which conforming HTTP/2 servers such as Node's reject.
firebase-admin/database throws a descriptive error on import: the Realtime Database client and its dependencies are omitted.
multipart/mixed responses, which no Admin API reads, fail with ERR_UNSUPPORTED_MULTIPART_RESPONSE instead of being parsed with @fastify/busboy into a response whose text and data getters throw.
Missing-dependency messages name vgoogle-cloud-firestore and vgoogle-cloud-storage.
Public declarations need no ambient Node types; Buffer is Node's Buffer where Node types are loaded, and httpAgent accepts any Node http or https Agent.

An app registry deletes only the exact instance it owns. Service instances use a Map, so prototype-named services do not collide. Closing an app prevents new services, coalesces concurrent deletion and attempts every cleanup even after a failure.

Forced token refreshes share one pending credential acquisition. Synchronous throws become rejected promises and allow retry. Token responses require a non-empty token and finite positive expiry; malformed-response diagnostics omit response contents.

App option snapshots preserve own prototype-named keys without mutating Object.prototype, detach null-prototype records, support deep records iteratively and reject ancestor cycles. Opaque credential/agent instances retain identity. FIREBASE_CONFIG accepts leading JSON whitespace.

CredentialDocument detaches validated JSON before authentication; frozen camel-case service accounts work and file changes cannot switch identity between validation and first use. New factory calls observe rotated file content. Malformed JSON errors preserve a sanitized SyntaxError without credential excerpts.

CredentialSession shares client discovery and token acquisition, retries failures and memoizes project/email lookups including an absent email. Access-token results contain only access_token and expires_in; empty tokens and non-finite or expired lifetimes are rejected.

Factories respect HTTP agent identity. JSON Google Auth clients receive the agent option that upstream omits. Certificate/refresh caches keep at most 64 entries per agent and kind, indexed by a SHA-256 digest rather than plaintext credentials.

Credential inputs must be plain acyclic JSON data with at most 64 nested containers; conflicting aliases and mismatched credential kinds are rejected. The legacy refreshToken tag is normalized to authorized_user. Generated key/protocol material and Google Auth provider implementations are retained dependencies.

Auth user, provider, timestamp and MFA records use explicit VPM projections. Serialization preserves own __proto__ and constructor claim names without writing Object.prototype or aliasing claim data. A bounded shallow walk and iterative fallback handle deep values and reports cycles; TOTP serialization detaches nested data while its public getter keeps the existing identity contract.

User-management plans detach update inputs, preserve prototype-named own keys without prototype writes, and snapshot deletion batches before asynchronous work. Oversized and sparse batches are rejected, and response error indices must be unique integers within the submitted batch. Provider linking cannot bypass unlink-array validation. Shared HTTP helpers, endpoint schemas and MFA conversion remain retained; Auth resource assembly and dispatch use VPM plans.

Auth token verification separates token-kind policy, per-call project identity and signature verification. The subject exemption for beforeSendSms/beforeSendEmail applies only to blocking-event tokens, not ID tokens or session cookies. Malformed legacy-token and audience shapes produce FirebaseAuthError diagnostics. Revocation captures auth_time before lookup, requires a finite numeric time when comparing against a revocation timestamp, and rejects invalid revocation timestamps. Crypto and key retrieval use the independently implemented JWT adapter over VPM dependencies.

Certificate/JWKS fetchers own immutable key snapshots and shared pending refreshes. Certificate freshness recognizes case-insensitive and quoted max-age, subtracts response age, respects no-cache/no-store, and prevents malformed or duplicate directives from creating an unbounded cache lifetime. Prototype-named JWKS key IDs remain own data. Verification without kid fetches keys once, retains the RS256/ES256 allowlist, and stops at the first verified key. Failed refreshes retry normally; noncacheable snapshots are not retained.

Auth request dispatch snapshots JSON-shaped input before asynchronous project discovery, gives each request its own headers, and encodes resource identifiers separately from endpoint templates. Concurrent project discovery is shared and failed discovery allows retry. Dot-segment identifiers and malformed Unicode are rejected. Non-JSON errors, non-string error codes and prototype-named unknown codes produce FirebaseAuthError diagnostics with response context instead of parse errors or TypeErrors.

HTTP/1 requests prepare URL, headers and body bytes once for all retry attempts. Caller mutations cannot change a retry payload. Header casing cannot overwrite an explicit content type; prototype-named headers remain own data, array values are detached, and each request option is read once. Response/decompression errors and premature closes settle the request instead of leaving it pending; failed streams are destroyed and buffered chunks released. Completed error responses preserve keep-alive reuse. Gzip/deflate coding is case-insensitive and Brotli responses are decoded. Common JSON/text response projection, shared retry policy and authorization headers use independent adapters.

HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 authorization captures transport options and detached header values before asynchronous token acquisition. The acquired bearer token overrides every casing of Authorization; explicit quota and metrics headers are recognized case-insensitively. Caller records and prototype-named header data are preserved, while app deletion is checked after token acquisition. Request body ownership remains with operation builders.

HTTP/2 attempts reuse owned URL/header/body plans across retries and set method/scheme/path from that plan. Response-less closure, aborted/error streams and invalid compression settle instead of remaining pending. Wire Content-Length is enforced even when the runtime accepts a mismatch, with HEAD and 304 representation lengths exempt. Coding is case-insensitive and supports Brotli; failures destroy the individual stream, not its batch session.

Each HTTP/2 session generation owns its error list. Old-session errors and GOAWAY events cannot enter a replacement session, observing the list cannot erase it, destroyed sessions are recreated and close is idempotent. Failed creation preserves prior diagnostics and allows retry.

HTTP response projection captures the low-level body once, detaches header records and arrays, and keeps JSON values and failures private. Valid scalar JSON, raw text, parse-error causes and HTTP diagnostic context retain their contracts. The parsed JSON object keeps its identity. Native RequestResponseError construction preserves subclasses; no obsolete prototype reset is needed on Node 24 or Bun. Multipart and raw-HTTP helpers remain retained.

Firestore configuration projects the credential and project from one app-options snapshot. The per-database registry owns the preferRest value used for construction instead of retaining mutable settings. Repeated initialization compares that value; failed construction is never cached. Public getFirestore/initializeFirestore routing, export bindings and underlying Google Cloud Firestore operations remain source-derived and separately tracked.

Storage owns its app/client context and projects project and credential from one options snapshot, including explicit projects with ADC. Emulator routing is passed to the client instead of mutating process.env; existing metadata, upload, download-URL and signed-form routes cannot be redirected by later environment changes. Explicitly named buckets also check app lifetime. A per-client endpoint resolver in vgoogle-cloud-storage keeps explicit API endpoints consistent across metadata and uploads and recognizes canonical default endpoints without incorrectly bypassing authentication. Entry-point wrappers and Storage operations remain separately retained.

implementation.kind: mixed: independent app, credential, used Auth, HTTP request/session/retry and authorization runtimes with independent JSON/text response projection, independent Firestore configuration/registry and Storage contexts and retained other helpers and service implementations
implementation.targetScope: App credentials, Auth, Firestore, Storage and messaging.

independentComponents.lib/app/lifecycle.js: Own registry with instance ownership, idempotent initialization and environment configuration. Existing credential/agent comparison diagnostics are retained.
independentComponents.lib/app/firebase-app.js: Own service Map and explicit active/closing/deleted lifecycle, with coalesced complete cleanup and failed-initializer recovery.
independentComponents.lib/app/token-lease.js: Own cached token lease and pending-acquisition ownership, with finite-expiry validation and retry after synchronous/asynchronous failures.
independentComponents.lib/app/options-snapshot.js: Own iterative snapshots and option comparison without prototype setters or recursive traversal.
independentComponents.lib/app/credential-internal.js: Own ADC and explicit JSON credential adapters over a shared CredentialSession. JSON validation and credential identity are separated from provider invocation; Google Auth remains a retained dependency.
independentComponents.lib/app/credential-factory.js: Own agent-aware credential pools with weak agent keys, 64-entry bounded JSON caches, digest-only keys and explicit ADC reset.
independentComponents.lib/app/credential-document.js: Own detached JSON credential documents, alias/type validation and sanitized file errors. A factory can read/validate one snapshot and pass that exact snapshot to authentication.
independentComponents.lib/app/credential-session.js: Own shared discovery/acquisition and per-credential memoization; forwards agent options to JSON clients and projects a validated two-field access-token result.
independentComponents.lib/auth/user-record.js: Own explicit read-only user/provider/metadata/factor projections and detached serialization, reusing the iterative snapshot walker. Diagnostic text and public response contracts are retained with attribution.
independentComponents.lib/auth/claim-snapshot.js: Own bounded shallow claim-copy path with iterative fallback, preserving own prototype-named keys, detached output and explicit cycle errors without unbounded recursion.
independentComponents.lib/auth/user-operations.js: Own operation plans for getUser, updateUser, revokeRefreshTokens and deleteUsers: detached request data, batch ownership and validated result accounting. Public diagnostics and wire fields remain source-informed; existing transport and endpoint schema validators are reused.
independentComponents.lib/auth/token-verifier.js: Own decode/policy/signature pipeline and per-call project resolution, preserving source-informed diagnostic contracts and token metadata. Cryptographic verification and certificate/JWKS retrieval use the independent utils/jwt adapter over VPM dependencies.
independentComponents.lib/auth/token-policy.js: Own token-kind claim checks and revocation comparison. Blocking-event subject exemptions cannot apply to ID/session tokens; authentication time is captured before asynchronous lookup and invalid comparison inputs are rejected.
independentComponents.lib/utils/jwt.js: Own certificate/JWKS fetchers, key routing, sequential no-kid verification and diagnostic adaptation over vjsonwebtoken/vjwks-rsa. Every signature path has the same RS256/ES256 policy; key acquisition callbacks settle once.
independentComponents.lib/utils/key-cache.js: Own immutable key snapshot and pending-refresh state, explicit freshness parsing, age accounting and retry. Malformed freshness directives do not produce NaN/Infinity lifetimes; noncacheable snapshots are not retained.
independentComponents.lib/auth/auth-request.js: Own resource URL construction, shared project discovery, detached request snapshots, per-request headers, emulator token selection and response/error dispatch. Endpoint validators remain retained; authorization uses the independent authorized-request adapter; diagnostic wording remains source-informed.
independentComponents.lib/utils/http-request.js: Own HTTP/1 request plan and one-settlement stream lifecycle: normalized headers, captured retry bytes, decompression, timeout/error teardown and keep-alive preservation. HttpClient retry orchestration in api-request.js uses the plan; the independent retry policy is shared by HTTP/1 and HTTP/2; response projection uses the independent http-response adapter.
independentComponents.lib/utils/request-retry.js: Own immutable retry policy, finite/integer option validation, strict Retry-After seconds and UTC HTTP-date parsing, explicit zero delays, capped exponential backoff and bounded native timer segments. Normal retry budgets and default statuses remain compatible.
independentComponents.lib/utils/authorized-request.js: Own captured transport options and header values before token acquisition, with one canonical credential/quota/metrics assembly shared by HTTP/1 and HTTP/2. Preserves post-token app-lifecycle validation and configured agent fallback; operation builders retain responsibility for body ownership.
independentComponents.lib/utils/http2-request.js: Own per-attempt HTTP/2 stream lifecycle over the shared captured request plan. Wire bytes remain stable across retries, pseudo-headers belong to the plan, close/error/decoder failures settle once, declared wire lengths are checked, and failed streams do not destroy the batch session. Http2Client orchestration reuses the independent retry policy and shared diagnostic adaptation; the session owner is implemented independently in http2-session.js.
independentComponents.lib/utils/http2-session.js: Own per-generation session records, diagnostic ownership and idempotent close. Late errors stay with their connection, returned error arrays are detached, destroyed sessions are recreated and failed connection creation can be retried without erasing the prior diagnostics. Native HTTP/2 provides protocol and socket behavior; diagnostic text remains source-informed.
independentComponents.lib/utils/http-response.js: Own JSON/text response projection with one body read, detached header records and array values, private eager JSON parsing state and native error subclass construction. The parsed JSON object and diagnostic request reference retain their identity contracts; diagnostic wording remains source-informed. Multipart and raw-HTTP parsing helpers are retained separately.
independentComponents.lib/firestore/firestore-internal.js: Own per-database client/configuration records and credential/project projection from one app-options snapshot. Settings getters are captured once, mutation cannot disguise conflicting initialization, and failed constructors leave no cached client. Lazy loading, project precedence, credential kinds, database identity and diagnostic text remain compatible; underlying Firestore operations and entry-point export routing remain retained.
independentComponents.lib/storage/storage.js: Own Storage facade with private app/client references, explicit credential/project configuration, default/named bucket selection and a real-app lifetime check for named buckets without copying app options. Lazy loading and diagnostic wording remain compatible; underlying Cloud Storage operations remain retained.
independentComponents.lib/storage/storage-context.js: Own one-snapshot credential/project projection and per-client emulator configuration. ADC receives an explicit app project. A weak client map preserves Firebase download-URL routing after environment changes without global mutation. The retained getDownloadURL entry point selects this context; the underlying SDK uses its independent endpoint resolver.

implementation.remainingWork: Multipart/raw-HTTP helpers, Auth endpoint schemas and other Auth methods, plus Firestore/Storage entry-point routing and helpers, plus the messaging service facade remain upstream-derived. Google Auth and underlying service client runtimes are tracked separately.

verification.applicationRuntime: Twenty-three focused tests on Node 24 and Bun, including isolated original app/credential controls, deep/shared options, provider/cleanup recovery, file rotation and actual signed-JWT/refresh-token OAuth POSTs through a local HTTP server and a counting agent.
verification.upstreamSuite: 6,062 retained upstream tests: Node 6,015 pass with 47 exact differences; Bun 6,000 pass with those 47 and 15 existing engine-wording differences. The additional difference requires the original global STORAGE_EMULATOR_HOST mutation, replaced by per-client configuration verified against two local servers. No upstream assertion is edited.
verification.callers: Identical 17 Auth/Storage/FCM requests, 25 Firestore RPCs and 17 results on Node 24 and Bun.
verification.credentialAdapters: 148 upstream app/credential tests pass on Node. Original controls reproduce agent-insensitive caches, omitted JSON-client agents, frozen-input mutation, validation/use identity drift, unsanitized parse errors and unbounded credential retention. Native local OAuth requests verify RSA signatures and both request bodies on Node and Bun.
verification.userRecords: 222 unchanged upstream record tests pass on Node; the complete 6,062-test suite retains the same existing differences on Node and Bun. 160 generated caller projections match upstream on both runtimes. Isolated controls reproduce prototype writes and constructor-claim aliasing in upstream serialization; VPM preserves keys and handles 20,000-level data without recursive traversal.
verification.userOperations: 166 unchanged upstream user-management tests pass on Node; the full suite retains only the existing exact differences on both runtimes. Local HTTP comparisons preserve normal requests and results, including partial deletion failures. Original controls reproduce batch mutation/sparse-list miscounts, invalid result indices, input mutation/prototype writes and provider-validation bypass.
verification.tokenPolicy: 228 unchanged upstream verifier and Auth verification tests pass on Node; the complete suite and real caller comparisons retain existing results on Node and Bun. Twelve locally signed token outcomes match. Isolated original controls reproduce ID/session subject exemptions, malformed-claim TypeErrors and nonnumeric/mutated revocation-time bypasses; VPM rejects them. No live credentials or live token service are used.
verification.keyVerification: 110 unchanged upstream JWT/key-fetch tests pass on Node. The full suite, fourteen focused tests and actual callers retain the existing results on Node and Bun. HTTP controls reproduce mutable keys, NaN/Infinity freshness, ignored age/directives and lost prototype-named JWKS IDs. Signed no-kid controls reproduce an unnecessary key fetch and acceptance of RS512 outside the normal allowlist; VPM fixes both.
verification.authRequests: 296 unchanged upstream request-handler tests pass on Node. The full suite and actual callers retain existing results on Node 24 and Bun. Separate original controls reproduce URL substitution/path/query injection, request/header mutation, duplicate project discovery and malformed server-error TypeErrors. Real local HTTP requests verify normal wire data, encoded identifiers and Auth error context.
verification.httpTransport: 93 unchanged upstream HTTP/1 and authorized-client tests run: 89 pass and four retain the existing exact multipart differences. Full Admin and Functions suites, sixteen focused tests and actual caller protocols pass on Node 24 and Bun with only the previously recorded differences. Local HTTP controls reproduce body/header changes on retry, overwritten Content-Type casing and pending promises after invalid gzip or truncated responses; replacement failures settle and keep-alive remains reusable after complete error responses.
verification.retryPolicy: Independent HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 retry policy checked against original-package controls on Node 24 and Bun, including mutated settings, nonfinite limits, complete seconds and UTC date grammar, zero and excessive delays, virtual long timers and an actual local HTTP retry. Complete suites and actual callers retain the documented outcomes.
verification.authorizedHeaders: Both authorized clients preserve token authority, explicit case-insensitive quota/metrics headers, captured options and detached array-valued headers. Separate original controls reproduce overrides and mutations; actual HTTP/1 wire requests confirm canonical values. App deletion remains checked after token acquisition. The full suites, eighteen focused tests, actual callers and packed consumers pass on Node 24 and Bun with their existing documented differences.
verification.http2Transport: 88 unchanged upstream HTTP/2 and authorized-client tests run with the existing exact differences; actual wire controls separately check assertions that upstream scheme expectations would stop before reaching. Original-package controls reproduce mutable retry bytes, duplicate Content-Type casing, response-less closure and gzip hangs, pseudo-header overrides, deterministic aborted/error ordering and Bun content-length mismatches. Node HTTP/2 servers serve both client runtimes; only the already documented upstream scheme colon is normalized for these other wire comparisons. No upstream assertions or mocks are changed.
verification.http2Sessions: Separate original/VPM process controls on Node 24 and Bun reproduce cross-generation diagnostics, mutable returned lists, reuse of destroyed sessions and lost diagnostics after failed recreation. The retained diagnostic messages and actual FCM caller protocol remain verified.
verification.httpResponses: Isolated original/VPM controls compare 24 JSON scalar/object, invalid/empty body and local HTTP success/error outcomes on Node 24 and Bun. They reproduce repeated body reads, header/array aliasing, public parse-state mutation and erased error subclasses. JSON object identity, request diagnostic references, parse-error causes and raw HTTP error context remain compatible. No upstream suite assertions change.
verification.firestoreFacade: Original/VPM controls on Node 24 and Bun reproduce mutable initialization settings and mixed project/credential snapshots, then verify captured getters, database identity and constructor failure recovery. Complete Admin/Functions suites, actual Firestore wire callers and packed public declaration consumers retain their documented outcomes.
verification.storageContext: Original/VPM controls on Node 24 and Bun use two local servers to reproduce cross-client emulator leakage, mixed metadata/upload endpoints and download-URL redirection. V2/V4 URLs and V4 form signatures, explicit ADC projects, one options snapshot and deleted-app bucket access are verified. The unchanged suite retains one new exact global-mutation difference; all actual caller protocols and archive consumers pass. The existing Storage signer/checksum suites and 25-request HTTP scenarios pass too.
